findings.issue_text: Server-side retrieval is gated only by a spoofable client-controlled Referer header check and a per-URL 60-second Redis throttle, with no global rate limit, no cap on topics created, and no cap on Redis keys, allowing the instance to be used as an on-demand scraper of the embedded host and enabling DB/app-server exhaustion and unbounded topic spam

RetrieveTopic jobs are enqueued on every cache miss without throttling or deduplication at enqueue time (the throttle lives inside the job), so the auto-reloading loading view (30s reload) causes one duplicate job per viewer per 30 seconds, flooding the Sidekiq queue with thousands of duplicate jobs that each burn a Redis round-trip and a DB exists? check

Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) downloads, parses, and imports the entire feed synchronously inside the RetrieveTopic worker thread for every embed miss, instead of being enqueued as a job and/or scoped to the requested URL

rss.items.each iterates every feed entry with no limit, so a first poll of a large feed runs thousands of PostCreator calls (cooking, indexing, callbacks) synchronously inside one scheduled job, and every hourly run re-iterates all items even when nothing changed

open-uri calls (topic_embed.rb:45 open(url).read and poll_feed.rb:31) have no timeout and no size cap, so a slow or hung remote host blocks a Sidekiq worker thread indefinitely (PollFeed has retry: false so it just hangs) and an arbitrarily large body is fully materialized in memory before parsing

feed_key is dead code — computed but never read or written — so no If-Modified-Since/ETag conditional fetch is implemented, causing the full feed to be re-downloaded and every item re-checked with a DB lookup plus SHA1 computation every hour even when nothing changed

Non-atomic setnx/expire in topic_retriever.rb can leave the throttle key with no TTL if the process dies between the two calls, permanently marking that embed_url as recently retrieved so non-staff users can never trigger retrieval for it; should use a single atomic SET key 1 EX 60 NX

Staff requests bypass the throttle entirely (no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)), so every staff pageview of an un-created embed re-runs the full retrieve path (remote fetch plus full synchronous feed poll) with no throttle until the topic exists

The raw_html cook method returns the raw string verbatim, bypassing the markdown/sanitizer pipeline, and content originating from external RSS feeds or scraped remote pages is stored and rendered unsanitized (raw post.cooked in best.html.erb), enabling stored XSS on the Discourse instance from a compromised or hostile feed/embeddable host

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server-side retrieval is gated only by a spoofable client-controlled Referer header check and a per-URL 60-second Redis throttle, with no global rate limit, no cap on topics created, and no cap on Redis keys, allowing the instance to be used as an on-demand scraper of the embedded host and enabling DB/app-server exhaustion and unbounded topic spam

adjudication.rationale: The new `/embed/best` endpoint enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil. Access control in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` relies on `request.referer` host matching `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, which is a client-controlled header and can be trivially spoofed. On the job side, `TopicRetriever` only throttles via Redis on a per-`embed_url` key for 60 seconds (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so an attacker can bypass it by varying the URL (different paths/querystrings) and continuously enqueue work. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `open(url).read` + Readability and then creates a topic/post (`PostCreator` with `skip_validations: true`) for each new URL, with no global rate limit or cap on topics/posts created. The Redis keys do expire after 60s (so not permanently unbounded), but the code still allows high-volume key creation and job/DB load and enables using the instance as an on-demand fetcher/scraper for the configured host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RetrieveTopic jobs are enqueued on every cache miss without throttling or deduplication at enqueue time (the throttle lives inside the job), so the auto-reloading loading view (30s reload) causes one duplicate job per viewer per 30 seconds, flooding the Sidekiq queue with thousands of duplicate jobs that each burn a Redis round-trip and a DB exists? check

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. The loading view (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`) reloads the page every 30 seconds, so each viewer will re-hit `#best` and enqueue another `retrieve_topic` job until the embed exists. There is no enqueue-time deduplication/keying in the diff. The only throttle is inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` (called from the job), which means duplicates still get queued and executed (at least doing URI parsing + a Redis `setnx` round-trip; and if not throttled they also do a DB `exists?` check). So the finding that this can create many duplicate Sidekiq jobs is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) downloads, parses, and imports the entire feed synchronously inside the RetrieveTopic worker thread for every embed miss, instead of being enqueued as a job and/or scoped to the requested URL

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly (not via Jobs.enqueue) when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed uses `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items.each`, importing each item, i.e., it downloads/parses/imports the entire feed synchronously within the RetrieveTopic job path for an embed miss. This is verifiable in the diff and can block the RetrieveTopic worker and repeat feed polling per distinct embed_url miss (throttled per URL, not per feed).

adjudication_records.issue_text: rss.items.each iterates every feed entry with no limit, so a first poll of a large feed runs thousands of PostCreator calls (cooking, indexing, callbacks) synchronously inside one scheduled job, and every hourly run re-iterates all items even when nothing changed

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `rss.items.each do |i| ... TopicEmbed.import(...) end` processes every item returned by `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no cap (e.g., `first(n)`) and no tracking of last processed item/etag/last-modified. On an initial run against a large feed, this can synchronously attempt to import every entry (calling `TopicEmbed.import`, which may invoke `PostCreator` for new URLs). On subsequent hourly runs it still iterates all items and computes content/sha1 and queries for each, even when nothing has changed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: open-uri calls (topic_embed.rb:45 open(url).read and poll_feed.rb:31) have no timeout and no size cap, so a slow or hung remote host blocks a Sidekiq worker thread indefinitely (PollFeed has retry: false so it just hangs) and an arbitrarily large body is fully materialized in memory before parsing

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces remote fetches via open-uri without passing any timeout or size-limiting options: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (topic_embed.rb) and `Jobs::PollFeed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (poll_feed.rb). Both will synchronously fetch remote content inside Sidekiq jobs/controllers and fully read the response body into memory (`.read` explicitly, and RSS parsing implicitly), with no cap on response size. Because no explicit timeouts are configured in these calls, a slow/unresponsive host can tie up the worker thread for an unbounded/very long period depending on Ruby/Net::HTTP behavior, and large responses can cause high memory usage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key is dead code — computed but never read or written — so no If-Modified-Since/ETag conditional fetch is implemented, causing the full feed to be re-downloaded and every item re-checked with a DB lookup plus SHA1 computation every hour even when nothing changed

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` computes a Redis/cache key (`"feed-modified:..."`) but that method is never called anywhere in the diff. The `poll_feed` method always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no conditional GET (no If-Modified-Since / ETag handling), so the feed will be fetched in full each run. It then iterates all items and calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which performs a DB lookup (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`) and computes a SHA1 of contents to detect changes, so this work repeats hourly even when the feed is unchanged.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic setnx/expire in topic_retriever.rb can leave the throttle key with no TTL if the process dies between the two calls, permanently marking that embed_url as recently retrieved so non-staff users can never trigger retrieval for it; should use a single atomic SET key 1 EX 60 NX

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, retrieved_recently? does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or loses connectivity after the SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE runs, the key will exist without a TTL, causing subsequent calls for that embed_url to always see setnx return false and thus treat it as “retrieved recently” forever for non-staff users. Using a single atomic `SET key val NX EX 60` (or a Lua script/transaction) would avoid this failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Staff requests bypass the throttle entirely (no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)), so every staff pageview of an un-created embed re-runs the full retrieve path (remote fetch plus full synchronous feed poll) with no throttle until the topic exists

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::RetrieveTopic, TopicRetriever is initialized with `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)`, and in TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? it immediately returns false when `@opts[:no_throttle]` is set, skipping the Redis 60s throttle. When EmbedController#best can’t find an existing TopicEmbed, it enqueues this job on every request. Until a TopicEmbed row exists, each executed job will run `perform_retrieve`, which (a) can synchronously run `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `feed_polling_enabled?` is true and then (b) does `fetch_http` via `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. So for staff-triggered requests, repeated views can cause repeated feed polling + remote fetch with no throttling until the embed is created.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The raw_html cook method returns the raw string verbatim, bypassing the markdown/sanitizer pipeline, and content originating from external RSS feeds or scraped remote pages is stored and rendered unsanitized (raw post.cooked in best.html.erb), enabling stored XSS on the Discourse instance from a compromised or hostile feed/embeddable host

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff explicitly adds a `:raw_html` cook method and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`). `TopicEmbed.import` and `import_remote` ingest external content (RSS `i.content` and scraped `Readability::Document#content`) and create posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. The embed view then renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, and for these posts `post.cooked == post.raw` (as asserted in the new spec), meaning externally-sourced HTML is rendered verbatim. For RSS imports there is no sanitization/whitelisting applied in this diff, so hostile feed content can become stored XSS in Discourse.
